head: e640162
summary: Removed the duplicate Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 7.1.2 declaration; clean compilation confirms the reported parity-test compiler errors no longer occur. Tagged five measured slow Persistence methods as heavy without changing assertions. Build and format pass; all 781 fast tests and all seven reclassified cases pass. Semantic replay produced 12 reports covering 1769 exchanges, with framework 29/39 (74.36%) and controls 4/4, unchanged from the skeleton baseline. Replay acceptance is board-only; deferred HTTP business/gateway groups remain red. No ported behavior or calculated figure changed. Head identifies the verified implementation/report commit before this status-only commit.
findings: NU1506: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 7.1.2 was declared twice across the Persistence and Sources/Auth/AI central-package sections. Removing only the duplicate fixes restore and compilation without changing the package graph.
The supplied CS1503/CS0246 parity-test diagnostics do not recur after package repair, including a full warning-as-error rebuild. No speculative namespace or project-reference edits were needed.
Five Persistence test methods measured 23.50-29.20 seconds during the integrated fast run. Their seven cases now carry the required heavy trait; unchanged assertions pass in a focused run.
A two-second startup probe timed out before readiness. A bounded retry of transient connection/timeouts succeeded; health/reset returned 200 and no helper remains.
The raw semantic replay board exactly matches the merged skeleton baseline. Deferred business/gateway endpoints remain red; this session claims board production, not complete HTTP parity.
